endorsements.quote: A local committee focusing on digital tool deployment should be convened to aid implementation.
The ability to seamlessly integrate the tools into the current workflows while avoiding redundant input of data into the EMR will likely encourage adoption by HCPs.

The design of digital tools should allow for the model to be updated and retrained to prevent overpredicting or underpredicting risk when the standard of care changes, such as with new, improved guidelines, evidence, or medications.

unlisted_practices: Demonstrate clinical value of digital tools through prospective trials showing improved patient outcomes before adoption.
Use robust large-scale clustered trials to assess the effect of digital tools on clinical outcomes.
Design digital tools to prioritize streamlined workflows with minimal user actions and reduce alert fatigue.
Monitor tool-specific key value metrics before and after integration of a digital tool.
Collaborate with patients during the design, study, and implementation of digital tools where appropriate.
Ensure patient diversity in datasets through federated databases and data harmonization to reduce bias and improve generalizability.
Allow customization of digital tools to the resources and needs of the community served.

screen.reason: Expert viewpoint discussing considerations, evidence, and workflow integration components for adopting digital algorithms and cardiovascular clinical decision-support tools.
